What it is: A three-layer process sandbox for AI agent terminal commands. Layer 1 — Interruptor: command firewall that blocks dangerous commands before execution. Layer 2 — PID namespace jail: contains blast radius via unshare. Layer 3 — systemd hardening: prevents kernel escape. Built from a real incident: a pytest MagicMock killed every process on the host via killpg(1, SIGKILL) — 56 gateway deaths/day.

2. The Incident That Started It All

July 19, 2026. A coding-hermes foreman ran pytest on gitreins-poc. A mocked MagicMock() object converted to integer 1, and the test called os.killpg(1, SIGKILL). PID 1 on Linux is init/systemd — every process owned by UID 1000 died together. Gateway, cron scheduler, Signal daemon, Docker containers, user shells, LSP servers, DuckBrain, Chimera — all gone.

Every diagnostic pointed at memory. OOM killer: 0 kills. systemd-oomd: 0 kills. dmesg: 0 kills. The real cause: a test framework killing the entire system, then the restart cycle repeating it every 2 minutes.

3. The Solution — Three-Layer Defense

LAYER 1: INTERRUPTOR — Command Firewall (v1.1.0, NEW)
  "rm -rf /"          → BLOCKED before execution
  "pytest"            → MODIFIED (auto-wrapped in sandbox)
  "echo hi"           → ALLOWED (passthrough)
         │
         ▼
LAYER 2: PID NAMESPACE JAIL
  unshare --user --pid --fork --kill-child=SIGKILL
  PID 1 inside jail = /bin/bash, not init
  kill -9 -1 kills only the sandbox
  Seccomp BPF denies 18 dangerous syscalls
         │
         ▼
LAYER 3: SYSTEMD HARDENING
  PrivateUsers, ProtectProc=invisible
  RestrictNamespaces=~pid, NoNewPrivileges
  Read-only filesystem, capability bounding set

5. Product Requirements

5.1 Problem Statement

AI coding agents run arbitrary shell commands. Every command is a potential system kill switch. Docker/VM/bubblewrap sandboxes focus on where code runs — they don't inspect what commands do. The agent still has a shell. The shell still has a PID namespace.

5.3 Competitive Landscape

ToolApproachTerminal-Jail Difference
just-bash (Vercel)TypeScript reimplementation of bash + overlay FSWrapper, not rewrite. Keeps real bash, adds kernel isolation.
ai-jail (963★)Rust + bubblewrap filesystem/network isolationCommand-level firewall. No container needed.
NVIDIA OpenShellProprietary YAML policy engineOpen source, zero deps, same concept.
KavachInterceptor with redirects/spoofsBlock/allow/modify. Three layers.
Unique angle: Most agent sandboxes protect files and network. Terminal-jail protects process namespace attacks — agents killing their own infrastructure. Filesystem isolation prevents data exfiltration; process namespace isolation prevents infrastructure self-destruction. Both are necessary.

8. PRD Document

Full PRD — problem statement, architecture, deployment, differentiation, 6 review questions

9. Review Questions (for external feedback)

  1. Does three-layer defense (firewall → namespace → systemd) cover the attacks you care about? What's missing?
  2. Is "replace $SHELL" the right integration point? Would a ptrace-based interceptor be better?
  3. Should the interruptor use a proper shell parser instead of regex patterns? Where does regex break?
  4. This is Linux-only. Is macOS support worth the complexity?
  5. Should --unshare-net be on by default? Does it break agent workflows?
  6. Should we add an overlay filesystem (like just-bash) or is systemd read-only root sufficient?
